record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.context_brief: Distinct distances between points and lines
record.original_question: Let L(m,n) be the minimum number of distinct distances between a set of m points and a set of n lines in the plane, where point-line distance is measured in the usual Euclidean way. Determine the asymptotic order of L(m,n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $P$ be a set of $m$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathcal{L}$ be a set of $n$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and a line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, let $d(p,\ell)$ denote the usual Euclidean (perpendicular) distance from $p$ to $\ell$. Define
$$D(P, \mathcal{L}) = \bigl|\{\, d(p,\ell) : p \in P,\ \ell \in \mathcal{L}\,\}\bigr|,$$
the number of distinct point-line distances determined by $P$ and $\mathcal{L}$, and set
$$L(m,n) = \min_{|P|=m,\ |\mathcal{L}|=n} D(P, \mathcal{L}).$$
Determine the asymptotic order of $L(m,n)$ as $m, n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. The best known lower bound, due to Sharir, Sheffer, and Smorodinsky, is $L(m,n) = \Omega(m^{1/5}n^{3/5})$ in a certain range of $m,n$, while no matching upper bound is known. Subsequent work (e.g., distinct distances on Pfaffian curves, 2025) treats related variants but does not determine the asymptotic order of $L(m,n)$.

status_evidence.title: Distinct distances between points and lines (Sharir, Sheffer, Smorodinsky)
status_evidence.snippet: For m points and n lines in R^2, the number of distinct point-line distances is Omega(m^{1/5} n^{3/5}) when m^{1/2} <= n <= m^2.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound is Omega(m^{1/5} n^{3/5}); matching upper bound is not established.

status_evidence.title: Distinct Distances on Pfaffian Curves (Natarajan, Sheffer, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on distinct distances on curves continues to investigate point-curve distance problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study related point-curve distance problems without resolving L(m,n).
